findings.title: Remus Stealer Markets Persistent Gmail Access: Hudson Rock Investigates
findings.summary_md: Hudson Rock examined Remus version 1.3.9 marketing, whose Mail feature let operators open a compromised Gmail inbox from a stolen-device record and claimed access survived password changes and session revocation. The developer described interaction with browser memory and said the malware runs then exits; a self-described customer reported access after browser closure, a session reset, and a password change. Hudson Rock said no controlled test showed fresh mail arriving after full account recovery and did not establish a Gmail zero-day.

findings.title: Remus Stealer advertises Gmail access that survives password changes
findings.summary_md: CyberInsider reported the same Remus version 1.3.9 Mail feature on November 9, including verification codes and account recovery links, and placed it in an Enterprise tier advertised at $1,000 per month. It relayed Hudson Rock's finding that the developer and a customer described access after browser closure and a password change, while no controlled test or Gmail vulnerability had been demonstrated. The article warned that an inbox can expose private correspondence, financial data, and password-reset messages for personal and workplace accounts.

findings.title: Remus malware claims Gmail access even after you change your password
findings.summary_md: Malwarebytes reviewed the Remus claims on November 11 and stressed that the promotional material showed a mailbox interface but did not prove retrieval of new messages after the account was comprehensively secured. It noted that Google documents password changes as invalidating access and refresh tokens, so token theft alone does not establish continued access. Its response guidance called for using a separate trusted device, disconnecting and cleaning the infected machine, reviewing signed-in devices and app access, and checking Gmail forwarding, filters, delegation, and recovery settings.

findings.title: Invoke RE on X: Remus Stealer Gmail stealer Chrome extension
findings.summary_md: Invoke RE reported on November 24 that Remus distributes a Gmail-stealing Chrome extension masquerading as Google Sheets. The extension reads Gmail through the browser's existing login session and posts message contents back to the attacker. The thread described a ZIP in the user's temp directory expanded by PowerShell, edits to Chrome's Secure Preferences registering extension ID cfmepkojgnkahbmgablgdahdomjdppgf, checks of Gmail account slots 0 through 9 through the unread Atom feed every minute, and exfiltration to prem1um[.]onl/m.
